hushfacebook.title: v0.18.0
hushfacebook.body:
Patching on a phone takes about a minute now, down from three. Reels get a 10 second skip when you double tap either edge, and a tap shows their controls without pausing. Hold a feed video for 2x, pinch a story or a profile photo to zoom, and pick your own background color for dark or light mode. You can also put your own words or a picture at the top of Home, save a GIF from a comment, and hide profile notes or the Related posts list. Reel captions keep the bottoms of their letters again too.

New in this release

- New patch, `Longer music on photo stories`, with its switch under Stories. Turn it on and a song you add to a photo for your Story plays for up to 30 seconds instead of 15 (issue #156, requested by @uk609x-gif). Videos keep Facebook's own lengths. It starts off. Checked on an emulator in the photo story editor, where the song's trim window covers 30 seconds with the switch on and 15 with it off. A posted story hasn't been tried yet.

- New patch, `Hide profile notes`, with its switch under News feed. Turn it on and the note bubble on profile pictures goes away, including the Drop a thought prompt that sits on your own picture (issue #195, requested by @JFG1000). The picture itself still opens when you tap it. It starts off. Checked on an emulator on your own profile, where the bubble is gone with no gap, a tap on the picture still opens its menu, and turning the switch off brings the bubble back. A friend's note is only checked in tests so far.

- New switch under Search, `Hide "People you may know" in search`. When you open search, the People you may know row Facebook puts there before you type doesn't show. Your recent searches stay, and For you keeps its own switch. It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off (issue #80, found from @MF-Debug's diagnostic report). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- New switch under Comments, `Tap anywhere on View more replies`. On some accounts only a tap right on the words of a View more replies row opens the replies, both in a post's comments and in the comments shown under a post in the feed. Facebook picks per account which of two layouts that row gets, and the switch gives every account the one where the whole row takes the tap. That layout spaces the row a little differently (issue #219, requested by @pseudoparenchymatous). It starts off. Checked in tests, and in a post's comments on an emulator, where a tap at the far end of the row opened the replies. The row under feed posts is checked in tests only so far.

- New switch under Stories, `Pinch to zoom`. Pinch a story, or a photo on someone's profile, and it grows under your fingers the way photos in the feed already do. Move your fingers to look around, and it goes back when you let go (issue #220, requested by @jonandeva). Photos in the feed keep Facebook's own pinch. It starts off. Profile and Page photos and stories were checked on a phone. A second switch under it, `Stay zoomed`, keeps the zoom when you let go (asked for by @lijovklm). Drag it with one finger or pinch again, then tap or press Back to put it back. A story stays paused the whole time. It starts off. On Page photos it was checked on Android 16, with Back, the back swipe and a tap each putting the photo back without leaving the Page. On a story it was checked on a phone too: the zoom stayed and the story stayed paused, a drag moved it around, and Back or a tap put it back without skipping to the next story.

- A third switch under `Pinch to zoom`, `Double tap to zoom`. Double tap a photo on someone's profile and it zooms in 2x around where you tapped. Double tap again to put it back (asked for by @lijovklm on issue #220). A single tap still opens the photo, a moment later than before, and stories keep their taps the way Facebook has them. It starts off. Checked on a phone on a profile's cover photo, where a scroll that starts on the photo still scrolls, and on a profile picture, where a press and hold opens the same menu with the switch on or off.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Newest reels first`. The Reels tab plays the newest posted of the reels Facebook has already loaded for you first, instead of its own pick. It can't fetch newer reels, so it's the newest of what Facebook picked for you (issue #134, requested by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi). It starts off. Checked in tests and on an emulator.

- New row under Appearance with the AMOLED black theme, `Background color`. Type a color code like #0D1117 and dark mode's backgrounds switch to it after Facebook restarts, with no repatch (issue #214, requested by @M7amma). Cards and menus get a slightly lighter shade of it. Grays up to about #535353 work, and a color too light for Facebook's text is refused with a note saying why. Leave it blank for the color you patched with. Settings backups carry it too. The row isn't there when Material You is in the same build. Checked on an emulator: Home, Menu, Marketplace, a post and its comments, and Facebook's settings all take the color, and a blank row brings back the patched one. The Hushfacebook settings page follows it too, with its cards and dialogs a shade lighter. On a light gray like #535353 its text and switches get lighter as well, so they stay easy to read.

- A second row next to it, `Light background color`, does the same for Facebook's light mode (issue #214). Type a light color code like #FFF8E7 and, after Facebook restarts, most of the feed takes it in place of white, and so do the Menu, your profile card at the top of it and Facebook's own settings. Gray buttons shift with it so they still stand out, and Facebook's text gets a little darker where it needs to so it stays easy to read. A color too dark for that is refused with a note naming the darkest gray it takes, #A6A6A6. Leave it blank for Facebook's own white. Settings backups carry it, and like the dark row it isn't there when Material You is in the same build. Checked on an emulator with #FFF8E7, where Home, the Menu and its profile card, a post's comments and Facebook's settings all took it, and dark mode looked the same as before.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hide the slow connection message`. When a video or GIF takes a while to load, the "This is taking a while. Try checking your network connection." message stops popping up, and the video keeps loading like before (issue #222, requested by @CiupaSs). It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- Two new switches under Menu, `Hide Help and support` and `Keep Settings and privacy expanded` (issue #224, requested by @sleeepingfatcat). The first takes the Help and support section out of the Menu. The second opens Settings and privacy with its rows already showing, and a tap on its header won't fold them away. Both start off, and the second takes effect after Facebook restarts. Checked on an emulator, where Help and support was gone and Settings and privacy opened with its rows out and its arrow pointing up. With the switch off it folds up like before.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Play whole reels in the feed's Reels row`. The reels in the Reels row on your Home feed keep playing instead of repeating their first second, so you can see what a reel is before you open it (issue #228, requested by @lijovklm). It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off. Checked on an emulator, where Facebook had told each tile to stop at one second and loop. With the switch on the tile played on for the whole recording.

- A GIF in a comment can be saved now. Press and hold a GIF comment and the menu that comes up has `Save GIF`, which saves the moving GIF to your Pictures folder, not the still frame the comment list shows (issue #226, requested by @pseudoparenchymatous). Facebook only offers Save photo for photo comments, so a GIF got nothing before. It comes with `Download any photo` and goes away when that's off. Checked on an emulator with two GIPHY comments, each saved as a full animated GIF.

- New patch, `Double tap to skip`, with its switch under Reels and Watch. Double tap the right edge of a reel to jump 10 seconds ahead, or the left edge to go back 10 (5 on one under 30 seconds). A double tap in the middle works like before (issue #225, requested by @lotslove). It's Facebook's own skip, which most accounts never get. It starts off. Checked on an emulator on a 1:36 video in the Reels tab, where each edge showed +10s or -10s and moved the video, and the like count didn't change. With the switch off the same double tap did nothing.

- New patch, `Tap shows the controls`, with its switch under Reels and Watch. A tap on a playing reel brings up its controls while it keeps playing, so you can reach the skip and mute buttons without stopping it (issue #225, requested by @lotslove). They go away on their own after 3 seconds, or right away on a second tap, and the button in the middle still pauses. Facebook built this layout and ships it turned off. It starts off. Checked on an emulator in the Reels tab, where a tap showed the controls around a pause button while the time kept moving, they hid about 3 seconds later or on a second tap, and the middle button paused the reel. With the switch off a tap paused it like before.

- New switch under News feed, `Hide "Related posts" under posts`. It takes away the Related posts list Facebook adds under some posts, the one whose titles are written by Meta AI. The post, its buttons and its comments stay (issue #231, requested by @MF-Debug). It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off. On an emulator with Facebook 584 the switch was asked about that list as the feed scrolled and answered it, with no crash. The account there doesn't get the list itself, so it hasn't been seen leaving a screen yet.

- New patch, `Home header text`, with its row under Appearance. Type a few words and they sit at the top of Home where the Facebook logo was, at the logo's height and in the colors Facebook gives its logo in light and dark mode (issue #230, requested by @schuani). Up to 30 characters, and a long line shrinks so it still fits beside the buttons. Leave it blank for Facebook's logo. Settings backups carry it. Checked on an emulator in dark mode over two fresh starts, where "Good morning" showed in white in the logo's place. The light mode colors are checked in tests. A second row, `Home header picture`, puts a picture of your own there instead, in its own colors. Pick one from your phone and a copy shrunk to fit is kept with Facebook's files, so the original can go. While it's chosen it takes the place of your words, and `Remove the header picture` brings back the words or the logo. Settings backups leave the picture out, since it can't travel in one. Checked on an emulator, where a picked picture showed at the top of Home with its shape kept, after the restart button and again after a fresh start, and the logo came back after Remove.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hold a feed video for 2x`. Press and hold a video playing in your feed or in Watch, the edge included, and it plays at double speed until you let go, the way a reel already can (issue #229, requested by @lijovklm). A video already at 2x or faster is left alone, and `Keep the video speed` doesn't hold on to the 2x once you let go. With `Long press opens comments` on, a hold on a feed video speeds it up instead. It comes with `Hold a reel for 2x`, works without that patch's switches and starts off. Checked on an emulator with Facebook 584, where holding the middle of a video in the Groups feed and then its left edge played it at 2x until the finger lifted, then back at normal speed, with nothing opening.

Fixes

- `Hide sponsored reels` also keeps ads out of the row of reels in the Home feed, the one you scroll sideways (issue #216, reported by @KingKode123). That row takes its ad tiles from a second ad pool of Facebook's, and only the Reels tab's pool was held before. Now that pool answers that it has no ad, so the row moves on to the next regular reel. On an emulator with Facebook 584 the row's pool was asked for an ad and gave none, with no crash, but that account showed no ad tile in the row to begin with, so an ad hasn't been seen leaving it yet.

- Reel captions don't lose the bottoms of their letters anymore (issue #96, issue #212). Facebook's Reels footer gives the caption a box a little taller than the space around it and cuts off what doesn't fit, so y, g and p and Bengali vowel signs got clipped on the last line, even in Facebook's own font. The space under the caption is empty, so the caption now draws into it. The first reel after Facebook starts gets it too. Checked on a phone over five fresh starts into Reels and six reels in a row, every caption whole, with the buttons beside it unchanged.

- `Menu tiles to hide` offers the Finds tile now, so it can go the way the others do. Facebook gives that tile no link of its own and has its server pick where it goes, so the list never saw it. A tile like that now goes by Facebook's id for the app behind it (issue #224, requested by @AlexanderQueen). Checked on an emulator, where Finds showed up in the list and left the Menu once ticked.

- Save on a story someone shared from Reels takes the reel now, not a picture of it. That kind of story is a still, the reel's first frame with a play button on it, and Facebook keeps the reel itself tucked inside the story as a sticker, so `Download any story` saved the still. It finds the reel there and saves its video at the best quality listed, named after the reel (issue #207, found from @jeiejs's diagnostic report). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you watched partway opens where you left off after Facebook restarts, not back at the first card. Someone who posted a new story after you watched the rest opens at the new one too. Facebook starts at the first card its servers think you haven't seen, and they never hear about these views, so the phone keeps the cards you watched for 48 hours and Facebook's pick skips past them. Your views still aren't sent, so you stay off the viewer lists (issue #218). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- `Turn off HDR brightness` no longer makes the phone's own video service crash and restart on a Samsung phone with a Snapdragon chip. HDR reels set off a tone-mapping step in that chip's video decoder, and that step is what crashed, so the decoder isn't asked to tone-map anymore. HLG reels still go over at the usual brightness, and PQ videos on that decoder play as Facebook set them up. Checked in tests, and on a phone over 30 reels with two HLG ones and no crash.

- With Debug logging on, Marketplace's report reads a whole page of search results again. Pages of 27 and 48 listings carried ads nested deeper than the report would follow, so it stopped early and called them incomplete. It follows more than twice as deep and reads four times as much of a page now, and when it does have to stop, it says whether the page was too deep or too big. Checked in tests, and on an emulator where both pages now read in full.

- With `Don't save search history` on, a search no longer sits at the top of search's Recent list until Facebook restarts. It already stayed out of your saved history, but Facebook still kept it in Recent for the rest of that session. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `Don't save search history` on, a page or profile you open from a search doesn't show up in your search history as "You visited" anymore (issue #221, requested by @itsmenewbie03). Facebook builds that entry from the visit report a profile sends as it opens, not from the search itself, so that one report isn't sent while the switch is on. The page opens the same as before. Checked on an emulator, where a page opened from its search result left nothing in the history.

- `Hide the reaction preview on posts` also takes away the "Name and 55 others" line beside the reaction faces, or the plain number Facebook puts there on some layouts. Only the faces went before. TalkBack still reads it. The number on the Like button stays until `Hide counts on posts` is on too, as its description says (issue #158). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- The `Mark as seen button` also shows when Facebook opens a story in one of its other story screens. Facebook 584 has three more besides the usual one, and the button only looked for that one. Checked in tests.

- A copy of Facebook made with `Clone app` could close right after it opened when the regular Facebook was installed beside it. It was asking the regular app for a saved value instead of asking itself, and Android doesn't let one app into the other's storage like that, so it closed the copy. Now every one of those requests goes to the copy's own storage (issue #16). Checked on an emulator.

- With `Material You theme` on in dark mode, the sheet that slides up when you tap the arrow beside your name in the Menu, the one for switching profiles, takes the theme's colors now. It stayed Facebook's own flat gray while the Menu behind it turned blue-gray. That sheet's gray comes with the screen from Facebook's server, paired with a light one, so no theme color ever reached it. A dark gray there now becomes the theme's gray at the same brightness, and the AMOLED theme keeps the sheet as it was (issue #37). Checked on an emulator, where the sheet went from #1F1F20 to the theme's #1E1F25.

- With `Picture-in-picture` on, leaving Facebook while the Hushfacebook settings were open over a reel floated the settings page in the small window. The reel kept playing under the page, so Facebook still opened its window on the way out. While the settings show, leaving Facebook doesn't open the window anymore, and once you close them it works the same as before. Checked on a phone, where leaving with the settings open over a reel opened no small window, and after closing them the reel went into the window as before.

Other changes

- Patching takes about a third of the time on a phone. Most patches used to read through all 215,000 of Facebook's classes to find the few they change, dozens of full passes in one patch. Now a single pass at the start notes what each class refers to, and a patch only reads the classes that mention what it's looking for. With the recommended patches on Facebook 584, a patch in Morphe Manager on a phone went from a little over 3 minutes on 0.17.0 to just under 1 minute, and on a desktop held to two cores from 54 seconds to 28. It still fits in the memory it needed before, and the patched app comes out the same as before, class for class (issue #216, reported by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi).

- `Use the system font` patches faster. It used to read through Facebook's code four separate times to find the places it changes, and it built the full name of every call and field along the way. It now makes one pass and only builds a name when the class matches one it cares about. On Facebook 584 with the recommended patches, `Use the system font` went from about 5.9 seconds to 1.5, and the whole patch from 51 seconds to 45 on a desktop. It still changes the same places in Facebook (issue #216, reported by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi).

Behind the scenes

- The device audit no longer refuses to start when the phone holds a settings backup from an older audit or the settings tool with no locale and theme saved beside it. It copies that folder off the phone first, takes the locale and theme the phone has now, and puts the backup's switches back at the end, the same as for a run that never finished. Twice on 2026-10-22 that backup had to be fixed by hand before a walk could run. Checked in tests, and the folder copy on a phone.

- A focused test run that names fixture tests after `:patches:fixtureTest` runs them again. Those filters used to be dropped, and the run passed without running a single fixture test.

- A push or a fixture check with a morphe-desktop CLI on the wrong patcher stops right away now. The 0.17.0 push ran its whole 17-minute gate with an old 1.18.1 CLI still set in the shell and only failed at the last step, because a bundle built on the 2.0 patcher won't load in a 1.x CLI. `scripts/pre-push.ps1` and `scripts/verify-all-patches.ps1` read which patcher the jar carries before anything heavy runs, and the message names the jar, both versions and, when it applies, the newer jar your user settings already point to.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `584.0.0.51.56`. On most phones that's build `475817393`, the arm64-v8a one.
3. Install over your current patched Facebook with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Facebook APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook#install).

Look over a diagnostic report before you share it. The filter can still miss private text it doesn't recognize.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 3718 runtime tests and 1181 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 102 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 584.0.0.51.56, the 64-bit build, and a second build of the same commit matched this bundle entry for entry. I patched Facebook with this exact bundle and walked the whole app with every switch on, on an emulator signed in to a full account. 76 of 103 hook families ran there, the new Home header text, Double tap to skip, Hide profile notes and Pinch to zoom among them. All 23 settings pages opened in dark and in light, and Facebook didn't crash once. Android's verifier raised nothing on the patched build, the same as on Meta's own. The walk doesn't reach downloads, chats or the story viewer, so those are covered by the patch tests alone this time.

repos.body:
Patching on a phone takes about a minute now, down from three. Reels get a 10 second skip when you double tap either edge, and a tap shows their controls without pausing. Hold a feed video for 2x, pinch a story or a profile photo to zoom, and pick your own background color for dark or light mode. You can also put your own words or a picture at the top of Home, save a GIF from a comment, and hide profile notes or the Related posts list. Reel captions keep the bottoms of their letters again too.

New in this release

- New patch, `Longer music on photo stories`, with its switch under Stories. Turn it on and a song you add to a photo for your Story plays for up to 30 seconds instead of 15 (issue #156, requested by @uk609x-gif). Videos keep Facebook's own lengths. It starts off. Checked on an emulator in the photo story editor, where the song's trim window covers 30 seconds with the switch on and 15 with it off. A posted story hasn't been tried yet.

- New patch, `Hide profile notes`, with its switch under News feed. Turn it on and the note bubble on profile pictures goes away, including the Drop a thought prompt that sits on your own picture (issue #195, requested by @JFG1000). The picture itself still opens when you tap it. It starts off. Checked on an emulator on your own profile, where the bubble is gone with no gap, a tap on the picture still opens its menu, and turning the switch off brings the bubble back. A friend's note is only checked in tests so far.

- New switch under Search, `Hide "People you may know" in search`. When you open search, the People you may know row Facebook puts there before you type doesn't show. Your recent searches stay, and For you keeps its own switch. It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off (issue #80, found from @MF-Debug's diagnostic report). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- New switch under Comments, `Tap anywhere on View more replies`. On some accounts only a tap right on the words of a View more replies row opens the replies, both in a post's comments and in the comments shown under a post in the feed. Facebook picks per account which of two layouts that row gets, and the switch gives every account the one where the whole row takes the tap. That layout spaces the row a little differently (issue #219, requested by @pseudoparenchymatous). It starts off. Checked in tests, and in a post's comments on an emulator, where a tap at the far end of the row opened the replies. The row under feed posts is checked in tests only so far.

- New switch under Stories, `Pinch to zoom`. Pinch a story, or a photo on someone's profile, and it grows under your fingers the way photos in the feed already do. Move your fingers to look around, and it goes back when you let go (issue #220, requested by @jonandeva). Photos in the feed keep Facebook's own pinch. It starts off. Profile and Page photos and stories were checked on a phone. A second switch under it, `Stay zoomed`, keeps the zoom when you let go (asked for by @lijovklm). Drag it with one finger or pinch again, then tap or press Back to put it back. A story stays paused the whole time. It starts off. On Page photos it was checked on Android 16, with Back, the back swipe and a tap each putting the photo back without leaving the Page. On a story it was checked on a phone too: the zoom stayed and the story stayed paused, a drag moved it around, and Back or a tap put it back without skipping to the next story.

- A third switch under `Pinch to zoom`, `Double tap to zoom`. Double tap a photo on someone's profile and it zooms in 2x around where you tapped. Double tap again to put it back (asked for by @lijovklm on issue #220). A single tap still opens the photo, a moment later than before, and stories keep their taps the way Facebook has them. It starts off. Checked on a phone on a profile's cover photo, where a scroll that starts on the photo still scrolls, and on a profile picture, where a press and hold opens the same menu with the switch on or off.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Newest reels first`. The Reels tab plays the newest posted of the reels Facebook has already loaded for you first, instead of its own pick. It can't fetch newer reels, so it's the newest of what Facebook picked for you (issue #134, requested by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi). It starts off. Checked in tests and on an emulator.

- New row under Appearance with the AMOLED black theme, `Background color`. Type a color code like #0D1117 and dark mode's backgrounds switch to it after Facebook restarts, with no repatch (issue #214, requested by @M7amma). Cards and menus get a slightly lighter shade of it. Grays up to about #535353 work, and a color too light for Facebook's text is refused with a note saying why. Leave it blank for the color you patched with. Settings backups carry it too. The row isn't there when Material You is in the same build. Checked on an emulator: Home, Menu, Marketplace, a post and its comments, and Facebook's settings all take the color, and a blank row brings back the patched one. The Hushfacebook settings page follows it too, with its cards and dialogs a shade lighter. On a light gray like #535353 its text and switches get lighter as well, so they stay easy to read.

- A second row next to it, `Light background color`, does the same for Facebook's light mode (issue #214). Type a light color code like #FFF8E7 and, after Facebook restarts, most of the feed takes it in place of white, and so do the Menu, your profile card at the top of it and Facebook's own settings. Gray buttons shift with it so they still stand out, and Facebook's text gets a little darker where it needs to so it stays easy to read. A color too dark for that is refused with a note naming the darkest gray it takes, #A6A6A6. Leave it blank for Facebook's own white. Settings backups carry it, and like the dark row it isn't there when Material You is in the same build. Checked on an emulator with #FFF8E7, where Home, the Menu and its profile card, a post's comments and Facebook's settings all took it, and dark mode looked the same as before.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hide the slow connection message`. When a video or GIF takes a while to load, the "This is taking a while. Try checking your network connection." message stops popping up, and the video keeps loading like before (issue #222, requested by @CiupaSs). It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- Two new switches under Menu, `Hide Help and support` and `Keep Settings and privacy expanded` (issue #224, requested by @sleeepingfatcat). The first takes the Help and support section out of the Menu. The second opens Settings and privacy with its rows already showing, and a tap on its header won't fold them away. Both start off, and the second takes effect after Facebook restarts. Checked on an emulator, where Help and support was gone and Settings and privacy opened with its rows out and its arrow pointing up. With the switch off it folds up like before.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Play whole reels in the feed's Reels row`. The reels in the Reels row on your Home feed keep playing instead of repeating their first second, so you can see what a reel is before you open it (issue #228, requested by @lijovklm). It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off. Checked on an emulator, where Facebook had told each tile to stop at one second and loop. With the switch on the tile played on for the whole recording.

- A GIF in a comment can be saved now. Press and hold a GIF comment and the menu that comes up has `Save GIF`, which saves the moving GIF to your Pictures folder, not the still frame the comment list shows (issue #226, requested by @pseudoparenchymatous). Facebook only offers Save photo for photo comments, so a GIF got nothing before. It comes with `Download any photo` and goes away when that's off. Checked on an emulator with two GIPHY comments, each saved as a full animated GIF.

- New patch, `Double tap to skip`, with its switch under Reels and Watch. Double tap the right edge of a reel to jump 10 seconds ahead, or the left edge to go back 10 (5 on one under 30 seconds). A double tap in the middle works like before (issue #225, requested by @lotslove). It's Facebook's own skip, which most accounts never get. It starts off. Checked on an emulator on a 1:36 video in the Reels tab, where each edge showed +10s or -10s and moved the video, and the like count didn't change. With the switch off the same double tap did nothing.

- New patch, `Tap shows the controls`, with its switch under Reels and Watch. A tap on a playing reel brings up its controls while it keeps playing, so you can reach the skip and mute buttons without stopping it (issue #225, requested by @lotslove). They go away on their own after 3 seconds, or right away on a second tap, and the button in the middle still pauses. Facebook built this layout and ships it turned off. It starts off. Checked on an emulator in the Reels tab, where a tap showed the controls around a pause button while the time kept moving, they hid about 3 seconds later or on a second tap, and the middle button paused the reel. With the switch off a tap paused it like before.

- New switch under News feed, `Hide "Related posts" under posts`. It takes away the Related posts list Facebook adds under some posts, the one whose titles are written by Meta AI. The post, its buttons and its comments stay (issue #231, requested by @MF-Debug). It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off. On an emulator with Facebook 584 the switch was asked about that list as the feed scrolled and answered it, with no crash. The account there doesn't get the list itself, so it hasn't been seen leaving a screen yet.

- New patch, `Home header text`, with its row under Appearance. Type a few words and they sit at the top of Home where the Facebook logo was, at the logo's height and in the colors Facebook gives its logo in light and dark mode (issue #230, requested by @schuani). Up to 30 characters, and a long line shrinks so it still fits beside the buttons. Leave it blank for Facebook's logo. Settings backups carry it. Checked on an emulator in dark mode over two fresh starts, where "Good morning" showed in white in the logo's place. The light mode colors are checked in tests. A second row, `Home header picture`, puts a picture of your own there instead, in its own colors. Pick one from your phone and a copy shrunk to fit is kept with Facebook's files, so the original can go. While it's chosen it takes the place of your words, and `Remove the header picture` brings back the words or the logo. Settings backups leave the picture out, since it can't travel in one. Checked on an emulator, where a picked picture showed at the top of Home with its shape kept, after the restart button and again after a fresh start, and the logo came back after Remove.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hold a feed video for 2x`. Press and hold a video playing in your feed or in Watch, the edge included, and it plays at double speed until you let go, the way a reel already can (issue #229, requested by @lijovklm). A video already at 2x or faster is left alone, and `Keep the video speed` doesn't hold on to the 2x once you let go. With `Long press opens comments` on, a hold on a feed video speeds it up instead. It comes with `Hold a reel for 2x`, works without that patch's switches and starts off. Checked on an emulator with Facebook 584, where holding the middle of a video in the Groups feed and then its left edge played it at 2x until the finger lifted, then back at normal speed, with nothing opening.

Fixes

- `Hide sponsored reels` also keeps ads out of the row of reels in the Home feed, the one you scroll sideways (issue #216, reported by @KingKode123). That row takes its ad tiles from a second ad pool of Facebook's, and only the Reels tab's pool was held before. Now that pool answers that it has no ad, so the row moves on to the next regular reel. On an emulator with Facebook 584 the row's pool was asked for an ad and gave none, with no crash, but that account showed no ad tile in the row to begin with, so an ad hasn't been seen leaving it yet.

- Reel captions don't lose the bottoms of their letters anymore (issue #96, issue #212). Facebook's Reels footer gives the caption a box a little taller than the space around it and cuts off what doesn't fit, so y, g and p and Bengali vowel signs got clipped on the last line, even in Facebook's own font. The space under the caption is empty, so the caption now draws into it. The first reel after Facebook starts gets it too. Checked on a phone over five fresh starts into Reels and six reels in a row, every caption whole, with the buttons beside it unchanged.

- `Menu tiles to hide` offers the Finds tile now, so it can go the way the others do. Facebook gives that tile no link of its own and has its server pick where it goes, so the list never saw it. A tile like that now goes by Facebook's id for the app behind it (issue #224, requested by @AlexanderQueen). Checked on an emulator, where Finds showed up in the list and left the Menu once ticked.

- Save on a story someone shared from Reels takes the reel now, not a picture of it. That kind of story is a still, the reel's first frame with a play button on it, and Facebook keeps the reel itself tucked inside the story as a sticker, so `Download any story` saved the still. It finds the reel there and saves its video at the best quality listed, named after the reel (issue #207, found from @jeiejs's diagnostic report). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you watched partway opens where you left off after Facebook restarts, not back at the first card. Someone who posted a new story after you watched the rest opens at the new one too. Facebook starts at the first card its servers think you haven't seen, and they never hear about these views, so the phone keeps the cards you watched for 48 hours and Facebook's pick skips past them. Your views still aren't sent, so you stay off the viewer lists (issue #218). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- `Turn off HDR brightness` no longer makes the phone's own video service crash and restart on a Samsung phone with a Snapdragon chip. HDR reels set off a tone-mapping step in that chip's video decoder, and that step is what crashed, so the decoder isn't asked to tone-map anymore. HLG reels still go over at the usual brightness, and PQ videos on that decoder play as Facebook set them up. Checked in tests, and on a phone over 30 reels with two HLG ones and no crash.

- With Debug logging on, Marketplace's report reads a whole page of search results again. Pages of 27 and 48 listings carried ads nested deeper than the report would follow, so it stopped early and called them incomplete. It follows more than twice as deep and reads four times as much of a page now, and when it does have to stop, it says whether the page was too deep or too big. Checked in tests, and on an emulator where both pages now read in full.

- With `Don't save search history` on, a search no longer sits at the top of search's Recent list until Facebook restarts. It already stayed out of your saved history, but Facebook still kept it in Recent for the rest of that session. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `Don't save search history` on, a page or profile you open from a search doesn't show up in your search history as "You visited" anymore (issue #221, requested by @itsmenewbie03). Facebook builds that entry from the visit report a profile sends as it opens, not from the search itself, so that one report isn't sent while the switch is on. The page opens the same as before. Checked on an emulator, where a page opened from its search result left nothing in the history.

- `Hide the reaction preview on posts` also takes away the "Name and 55 others" line beside the reaction faces, or the plain number Facebook puts there on some layouts. Only the faces went before. TalkBack still reads it. The number on the Like button stays until `Hide counts on posts` is on too, as its description says (issue #158). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- The `Mark as seen button` also shows when Facebook opens a story in one of its other story screens. Facebook 584 has three more besides the usual one, and the button only looked for that one. Checked in tests.

- A copy of Facebook made with `Clone app` could close right after it opened when the regular Facebook was installed beside it. It was asking the regular app for a saved value instead of asking itself, and Android doesn't let one app into the other's storage like that, so it closed the copy. Now every one of those requests goes to the copy's own storage (issue #16). Checked on an emulator.

- With `Material You theme` on in dark mode, the sheet that slides up when you tap the arrow beside your name in the Menu, the one for switching profiles, takes the theme's colors now. It stayed Facebook's own flat gray while the Menu behind it turned blue-gray. That sheet's gray comes with the screen from Facebook's server, paired with a light one, so no theme color ever reached it. A dark gray there now becomes the theme's gray at the same brightness, and the AMOLED theme keeps the sheet as it was (issue #37). Checked on an emulator, where the sheet went from #1F1F20 to the theme's #1E1F25.

- With `Picture-in-picture` on, leaving Facebook while the Hushfacebook settings were open over a reel floated the settings page in the small window. The reel kept playing under the page, so Facebook still opened its window on the way out. While the settings show, leaving Facebook doesn't open the window anymore, and once you close them it works the same as before. Checked on a phone, where leaving with the settings open over a reel opened no small window, and after closing them the reel went into the window as before.

Other changes

- Patching takes about a third of the time on a phone. Most patches used to read through all 215,000 of Facebook's classes to find the few they change, dozens of full passes in one patch. Now a single pass at the start notes what each class refers to, and a patch only reads the classes that mention what it's looking for. With the recommended patches on Facebook 584, a patch in Morphe Manager on a phone went from a little over 3 minutes on 0.17.0 to just under 1 minute, and on a desktop held to two cores from 54 seconds to 28. It still fits in the memory it needed before, and the patched app comes out the same as before, class for class (issue #216, reported by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi).

- `Use the system font` patches faster. It used to read through Facebook's code four separate times to find the places it changes, and it built the full name of every call and field along the way. It now makes one pass and only builds a name when the class matches one it cares about. On Facebook 584 with the recommended patches, `Use the system font` went from about 5.9 seconds to 1.5, and the whole patch from 51 seconds to 45 on a desktop. It still changes the same places in Facebook (issue #216, reported by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi).

Twice on 2026-10-22 that backup had to be fixed by hand before a walk could run. Checked in tests, and the folder copy on a phone.

hushmessenger.body:
### Reported issues

- [#69](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/69) New **Quiet incoming calls** switch under Conversations. Calls still come in, but Messenger doesn't ring, vibrate or pop the call up over what you're doing. The call waits in the notification shade with its Answer and Decline buttons, and a call you miss still shows up in the chat. If the Facebook app is on your phone, it can still ring for the same call. It starts off.

New messages used to push them below the four rows your launcher shows until you next opened and left Messenger. Android 9 and 10 still put them back only when Messenger opens or closes.

- A video picked in a chat whose access ran out before or during the send no longer gets **Fix videos that won't send** marked as failing in settings. It goes out the way Messenger would send it anyway.
- If the phone's sound encoder won't start while a video's sound is being fixed, it's let go right away instead of staying held until Messenger closes.
- The copies **Fix videos that won't send** makes of videos you pick now go a day after their last use, even if you never pick another video or you've turned the switch off. Messenger clears them when it starts and again while it's open as each one's day runs out. They used to sit in Messenger's cache until the next pick.

Skipped choices and Auto reply staying off used to run past the end of that message. Now the whole result stays written under the backup buttons.
- When reading a choices file takes too long, the message says your choices didn't change. It used to warn that a saved file may be cut off, which is only true when saving one.
- If settings can't open from the side menu or the Messenger logo, two short messages now say so and then name the other way in. One message was too long and lost its second half.
- Picking a font file while **Use your own font** is off now says to turn the switch on, instead of telling you to restart Messenger. The file's name stays on the line under the button, where a long one can't push the rest off the message.

Undo leaves alone any switch you flipped yourself after the change.

- On a Root Mount install, **Patch controls** and **Restart Messenger** never actually showed up on Messenger's icon. Android turned down the icons they used. They show up now.
- Each way back into settings now has its own switch on the App tab, as asked in [HushFacebook#146](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFacebook/issues/146). - Some accounts get Meta's newer AI agent tab in the bar where the Meta AI tab usually sits. **Hide Meta AI** now hides that one too, and the bar still lights up the right tab. Restart Messenger to see it go.

Messenger's very first start turned them on, and they stayed there until you opened Messenger a second time. Updating over an existing install never did this.

Accounts that get more than one sticker maker see that button instead of **Generate AI stickers**, and it opens a menu with AI stickers in it, so the switch used to miss it. The custom and music stickers in that menu are hidden along with it while the switch is on.
- With **Hide AI sticker tools** on, the rest of the Suggested row now moves up to fill the spot where **Generate** or **Generate AI stickers** used to sit. The button went away before, but its slot at the start of the row stayed blank.

### Docs

- The README's troubleshooting list now covers a cloned Messenger showing the settings icon again, chats and calls notifying twice because of the Facebook app, and restoring chats with a PIN when the Google Drive restore errors out.

### Checks

- A release can't go public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before the tag or GitHub if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Messenger crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` does that walk. It patches Messenger from the bundle, installs it in place on a leased phone or an emulator, opens both settings pages, a chat and the patched screens, then reads the crash buffer and writes the receipt publish asks for. - A Gradle run through this PC's build wrapper fails when the wrapper itself errors out before Gradle starts. It used to exit 0 and read as a pass.
- Recording a Messenger build with `CompatReport.java --save` refuses an APK that isn't signed by Facebook or Meta, or whose signer apksigner can't read. The release build stage also checks each stock APK against the checksum in its record before patching it, and CompatReport looks for Python as `py`, `python3` or `python` (never the Windows Store stub) instead of assuming `python`.

Messenger's very first start turned them on, and they stayed there until you opened Messenger a second time. Updating over an existing install never did this.
- **Hide AI sticker tools** now hides the plain **Generate** button at the start of the sticker keyboard's Suggested row too. Accounts that get more than one sticker maker see that button instead of **Generate AI stickers**, and it opens a menu with AI stickers in it, so the switch used to miss it. The custom and music stickers in that menu are hidden along with it while the switch is on.
- With **Hide AI sticker tools** on, the rest of the Suggested row now moves up to fill the spot where **Generate** or **Generate AI stickers** used to sit. The button went away before, but its slot at the start of the row stayed blank.
- HushMessenger is now built for Morphe's 2.0 patcher, so this release needs **Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer**. Update Manager first, then repatch. Every patch still applies to Messenger 584 and the patch count is the same.

### Docs

- The README's troubleshooting list now covers a cloned Messenger showing the settings icon again, chats and calls notifying twice because of the Facebook app, and restoring chats with a PIN when the Google Drive restore errors out.

### Checks

- A release can't go public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before the tag or GitHub if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Messenger crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` does that walk. It patches Messenger from the bundle, installs it in place on a leased phone or an emulator, opens both settings pages, a chat and the patched screens, then reads the crash buffer and writes the receipt publish asks for. Any Messenger crash fails the walk. Leaving out a page or a screen makes it partial, and neither one backs a release. The receipt also names the APK patched from the bundle and the one the phone actually ran, and publish wants them to match, so walking whatever was already installed (`-SkipPatch`) only counts when it's that same APK. A crash buffer the walk can't read fails it, and the script exits 0 only for a pass (2 for partial, 1 for a fail). A walk that finds the device busy keeps the APK it patched, so the next try goes straight to the device instead of patching again.
- The development release check, the one a held build goes through, fails when the source has no bundle timestamp. Before, a bundle and a source both missing one counted as a match there. The full release check already refused it, and now it says why.
- A Gradle run through this PC's build wrapper fails when the wrapper itself errors out before Gradle starts. It used to exit 0 and read as a pass.
- Recording a Messenger build with `CompatReport.java --save` refuses an APK that isn't signed by Facebook or Meta, or whose signer apksigner can't read. A record pins the APK's checksum, so a re-signed copy could have been written down as the stock build. The release build stage also checks each stock APK against the checksum in its record before patching it, and CompatReport looks for Python as `py`, `python3` or `python` (never the Windows Store stub) instead of assuming `python`.

hushfeed.title: v0.79.0
hushfeed.body:
Hushfeed v0.79.0 has 141 patches. 140 of them are for global TikTok 47.5.3 (`com.zhiliaoapp.musically`), and 95 work on PineDrama 47.5.3, one of those made just for it. It needs Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer, since it's built on patcher 2.0.0.

TikTok stays on 47.5.3, so the TikTok APK you already have is fine to patch again. PineDrama moves to 47.5.3, so grab that one from APKMirror before you patch it. PineDrama got a lot of attention in this one. Six more patches run on it, and photo comments and imported fonts work there now. On TikTok there's a spam comment filter and a way to record a LIVE straight off the screen, and `Hide videos you have already seen` keeps watched videos out of For You again.

Here's every report this release changed something for, and what changed.

For bug reports

* Repeats in For You (#172). `Hide videos you have already seen` checks each new For You page once TikTok hands it over, so videos you watched stop coming back.
* The comment bar on photo posts (#171). With `AMOLED dark theme`, the `Add comment...` bar under a photo post is black instead of letting the photo show through.
* Fonts on PineDrama (#243). `Use an imported font` now draws PineDrama's text in your font, and bold text stays bold.
* Missing saved stickers (#214). PineDrama's sticker panel loads every sticker you saved. It used to stop at 100.
* Low download quality (#240). When the quality list stops below 720p, it also offers the video's own H.264 or HEVC file if that one is taller, and the diagnostic report shows why each quality was or wasn't offered.
* Commenter countries (#201). `Show where commenters are from` remembers people's countries from their earlier comments and videos, so it finds one more often.
* Running out of memory while patching (#220). The README says to give morphe-desktop 2 GB with `java -Xmx2g`.
* Automatic Clear display (#84). A search result you open again clears again, even if you brought its buttons back by hand last time.

For feature requests

* PineDrama (#156). It moves to 47.5.3, six more patches run on it, and a new `Allow photo comments` patch lets the comment box ask TikTok's server about photo comments like TikTok does. Hushfeed's settings also say to restart PineDrama now, not TikTok.
* A spam shield for comments (#187). `Hide spam comments` hides the bots that point you to their bio or hand out a contact, and leaves the creator's own comments alone.
* Effects that refuse older phones (#176). `Report a newer phone to effects` tells the effects server you have a Galaxy S24 Ultra.
* Saving LIVEs (#37). `LIVE recording source` can record the screen as you watch, and Share > Video quality now shows in gaming and football rooms too.
* LIVE recording presets (#203). `LIVE recording quality` offers Original, 1080p, 720p, 540p and 360p and takes a room's 60 fps stream when it has one. You can change it from a LIVE room's Share sheet too.
* The liquid glass bar (#231). `Blur the video behind the bar` frosts the pill with the video under it, and the lens slides between tabs every time now.
* Dark LIVE rooms (#159). The light bits left in rooms turn dark, from the profile card's tiles to the menu's navigation bar, and a room stays dark when your phone switches themes.
* The Auto scroll switch on foldables (#234). `Hide TikTok's Auto scroll button` hides the switch beside the avatar too, with or without Auto-advance.
* OmerKurdi79's batch (#232). Clear display lets go with your swipe, and the See-through bottom bar no longer drops the caption over the tabs after each swipe.
* An instant pause (#239). With double tap set to do nothing, a tap pauses or plays the moment your finger lifts.
* Latest on Following (#226). `Latest first` keeps everything below your video in date order as posts load, and the tab starts on the newest post.
* Better sorting (#180). Profile grids get Least viewed first and Least liked first. While an order is on, the grid loads up to 300 videos by itself, and swiping through them keeps that order.
* Stories from LIVE creators (#233). `Open the Story when a creator is LIVE` opens their Story from their profile picture or your chat with them, and the next tap joins the LIVE.
* LIVE quality in dark mode (#57). The newer Video quality picker in a LIVE room's menu is readable on dark mode.
* Add to Story (#88). `Allow Add to Story anyway` brings the button back when a creator turned off content reuse.
* Time zones (#184, #198). With `Match locale and timezone` on, chat dates follow the preset's zone.
* Thoughts (#186). `Turn on Thoughts` shows Thoughts for accounts TikTok left out.
* Original image formats (#229). Stickers that don't move are saved as TikTok sent them too.
* Camera brightness (#200). `Keep the screen's brightness in the camera` also covers the front flash and the fill light.
* Region locked features (#98). Feature Gate Lab's `Scrolling comments on videos` preset says up front that only some videos get scrolling comments.

## What's changed

* On PineDrama, Hushfeed's settings now tell you to restart PineDrama instead of TikTok. That covers the note under each switch, the restart button that shows up once you flip one, the saved message and the Feature Gate Lab, in English and all nine translations. Other mentions of TikTok, like its servers or the TikTok Sans font, stay as they are (#156).
* New `Hide spam comments` switch in Hushfeed settings > Comments, off by default (#187). It hides bot comments that send you to their profile or a "link in bio", spell out a website, hand out a Telegram or WhatsApp contact, or offer free followers. It knows the common phrasings in English and the languages Hushfeed's settings come in, plus French. Your own comments stay, and so do the creator's and any they pinned or liked, so a "part 2 in my bio" from the creator still shows.
* `Hide videos you have already seen` takes watched videos out of For You again (#172). TikTok reads each new page once before handing it to the feed. The switch sits that first read out, as it does on lists you open yourself, but everything the read kept was then remembered as allowed and never checked again. Now the page gets checked against what you've watched once TikTok hands it over, and your watch record starts loading during that first read so it's ready in time.
* With AMOLED dark theme, the `Add comment...` bar under a photo post you open from search, a profile or a link is black now (#171). TikTok leaves that bar see-through, and a photo runs on underneath it, so the photo showed through where a video post shows black.
* `Use an imported font` now works on PineDrama (#243). PineDrama doesn't carry TikTok's own fonts, so its text fell back to your phone's font and the imported one never got used. It now draws in your font at the weight the app asked for, so bold text stays bold.
* Feature Gate Lab's `Scrolling comments on videos` preset tells you before you apply it that comments only scroll on videos TikTok has turned them on for. Each video carries its own flag from TikTok's server, so most videos look the same with the preset on (#98).
* New `Allow photo comments` patch for PineDrama, with its switch off by default (#156). PineDrama hides the gallery tab in the comment box for everyone, even though TikTok's server allows photo comments. Turn the switch on in Hushfeed settings > Comments and restart, and the comment box asks the server like TikTok does.
* PineDrama moves to 47.5.3 and 47.4.3 is dropped, so grab the new PineDrama from APKMirror before you patch it again. Six more patches run on it now: `Advanced downloads`, `Automatic video advance`, `Hide inbox items`, `Hide profile shortcuts`, `Open the comments at full height` and `Show the progress bar`. PineDrama 47.5.3 has no stories, HD upload choice or foldable comment panel, so `Story controls`, `Always upload in HD` and `Foldable split comment view` are TikTok only now. That makes 95 patches Morphe Manager offers for PineDrama. The rest lean on TikTok's LIVE rooms, feed buttons or resources that PineDrama doesn't have (#156).
* New `Report a newer phone to effects` switch, off by default (#176). Effects ask TikTok's server whether your phone can run them, and on some older phones the answer is "This effect doesn't work on this device". With the switch on, the effects server is told you have a Galaxy S24 Ultra. Sign-in and everything else still see your real phone. An effect your phone really can't run may still fail or look wrong.
* New `Load all saved stickers` patch, with no switch. PineDrama's sticker panel loaded only the first 100 stickers you saved and never asked for more, so the rest were missing from Saved. It now asks for all of them in one go. TikTok gets the same first request, and it still loads more by itself past that (#214).
* New `LIVE recording source` choice under `Record LIVEs you watch`. `Stream only` saves the room's own video like before. `Screen` records what your phone shows while you watch. Android asks to allow screen recording each time, and Stop saves it. The app's sound comes along when TikTok has the microphone permission, otherwise the recording is video only (#37).
* New `Blur the video behind the bar` switch under `Liquid glass look`. It frosts the glass pill with a soft blur of the video behind it, off by default, on Android 12 and up (#231).
* With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, the light pieces left in a LIVE room go dark too. The navigation bar under the menu a long press in a room opens stays dark now, even when TikTok turns it light again. The tiles in the host's profile card and the fan club's tab strip and card turn dark, and the text and icons on them turn light so they stay readable (#159).
* `Tag saved videos with their details` now tags the videos TikTok actually sends. Their files carry a short list of TikTok's own fields where the tags go, and the switch left those files alone, so every save came out with no title, creator, date or link. The tags go in now, and TikTok's fields stay in the file beside them.
* `Hide TikTok's Auto scroll button` also hides the Auto scroll switch that tablets and unfolded foldables show beside the avatar on each video, and it works with `Auto-advance videos` off now. Before, that switch stayed, and the hide only worked while Auto-advance was on (#234).
* The README's install steps now say which 47.5.3 file to get. Morphe Manager on a phone should patch the bundle (`.apkm`), because on a device with 3 GB Manager ran out of memory on the APK and patched the bundle in about a minute. A computer should patch the APK. The out of memory tip under Patching stalls partway points to the bundle too, and step 6 says to uninstall the Google Play TikTok first, which logs you out.
* With `Keep Clear display across videos` off, the tabs, the caption and the buttons now come back as your swipe lets go, so the next video arrives with them. Before, it settled full screen first and then jumped when they showed up again. A Clear display you turn on from TikTok's long-press menu also stays on now instead of switching itself off as the menu closes (#232).
* With `See-through bottom bar` on, the caption, the buttons and the search bar don't drop down over the tabs for a moment after each swipe anymore (#232).
* Long press set to `Save the frame on screen as a photo` works again on 47.5.3. TikTok's player now draws each video into a layer of its own under the feed, so the save only found an empty view and said the frame couldn't be read. It reads the player's layer now, and the photo comes out at the video's own size with no caption or buttons, on the feed and on videos opened from a profile.
* `Remove feed ads` also takes out the smaller Lemon8 card in For You, the one titled "Your daily dose of inspiration" with a Lemon8 post and Open Lemon8 under it. It's built differently from the full-screen Lemon8 card the switch already removed, so it slipped through on 47.5.3.
* The `Show how many were filtered` label and the `Show what is left of the budget` label stay off the Shop tab and the Nearby tab now. Both showed there because the Home tab stays selected on those tabs, and the filtered count sat right over their search boxes. They still show on For You and Following.
* With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, a room's viewer ranking opens dark again. A shop room's Top customers ranking still keeps TikTok's light look, because its tab titles came out dark on dark (#159).
* The README says how much memory morphe-desktop needs on a computer. With every patch picked on 47.5.3 it runs out at 1 GB, Java's default on a 4 GB machine, and finishes at 1.5 GB, so start it with `java -Xmx2g` (#220).
* With `Double tap` set to `Do nothing`, or every corner of `Double tap by corner` set to it, a tap on a video pauses or plays the moment your finger lifts. TikTok used to hold each tap for a beat in case a second one followed, and two quick taps counted as a double tap that did nothing. Now each one counts (#239).
* The build uses Gradle 9.8.2, up from 9.7.1. The build files now name the Guava advisory by its CVE number, CVE-2026-102554, because GitHub's global advisory database doesn't list its GHSA id.
* The README now lists the parts of Hushfeed's settings that an add-on bundle patched in beside it can count on, and a test fails if one of them changes. Anything else in the settings code can still move between releases.
* What's new now carries only the newest releases' notes, and its Full changelog button has the rest. Every release since 0.60.0 used to be built in, in all nine languages, and those notes alone were about 14% of the extension's size.
* `Glass lens on the current tab` slides to the next tab even after you've sat on one tab for a while, or when TikTok takes a moment to open a tab for the first time. Before, it only slid when you tapped quickly, and in both of those cases it jumped instead (#231).
* With `Automatic Clear display` on, a search result you open again from TikTok's own search clears again, even when you brought its buttons back by hand the last time you watched it. Before, it remembered that and stayed uncleared (#84).
* `LIVE recording quality` also offers the presets from a LIVE room's own quality menu: Original, 1080p, 720p, 540p and 360p. If the room doesn't have the one you picked, the recording takes the closest one below it, or the closest above when nothing lower is there. A room's 60 fps streams count as the quality they're in, so 1080p in a 1080p60 room records the 60 fps stream instead of falling back to 720p (#203).
* When the Download quality list stops below 720p, it now also offers the video's own H.264 or HEVC version if that one is taller. The diagnostic report has a new section for the last video you opened the list on, with each quality it offered and why any others were left out (#240).
* `Show where commenters are from` finds a country more often. It remembers someone's country from their earlier comments and from videos of theirs you scrolled past, and it reads one more of the country fields TikTok sends with an account (#201).
* `Latest first` on the Following tab now keeps everything below the video you're watching in date order as more posts load. A newer post that shows up late moves up right after your video, and nothing you've already scrolled past moves. It also asks TikTok for twice as many posts on the first load, so a newer post is less likely to turn up after the first video is already playing. When TikTok opens fresh, it no longer starts the Following tab on the post it saved from last time, which was usually older than everything loading under it. The first video now comes from the new, sorted list (#226).
* Sorting a profile or Liked grid now has Least viewed first and Least liked first. While an order is on, the grid keeps loading by itself (up to 300 videos) so the order covers more than the first screen, and a button in the grid's corner changes the order right there. When you open a video from a sorted grid, swiping up goes on in the grid's order too, where it used to follow TikTok's. On the Liked tab the button sits under TikTok's note about who can see your liked videos instead of covering it (#180).
* New switch under `Remove avatar rings`: `Open the Story when a creator is LIVE`. When someone who's LIVE also has a Story, tapping their picture on their profile or on your chat with them in the Inbox opens the Story, and tapping it again joins the LIVE. It starts off (#233).
* With `Record LIVEs you watch` on, a LIVE room's Share sheet has a `LIVE recording quality` row. Tap it to pick the quality the next recording uses without going to Hushfeed settings (#203).
* With `Offer LIVE quality in more rooms` on, Share > Video quality also shows in gaming and football LIVE rooms. TikTok left it out of LIVE Studio rooms and rooms that support low latency (#37).
* In dark mode, the newer Video quality picker in a LIVE room's menu is readable again. Its rows sit on a white card, and Original, 1080p and the rest came out light on it, so they were hard to make out. They turn dark on the card now (#57).
* With `Dark LIVE panels in dark mode` on, a LIVE room stays dark when your phone switches between light and dark while the room is open. Before, its Share sheet opened white until you left and came back (#159).
* New switch under Share sheet: `Allow Add to Story anyway`. When a creator turned off content reuse, it brings back Add to Story in the share sheet (the button in the row of actions and your story's bubble at the start of Send to) and on their stories, like `Allow Duet and Stitch` does for those two. TikTok may still refuse the post (#88).
* With Region spoof's `Match locale and timezone` on, chat date headers follow the preset's time zone now instead of the phone's clock (#184, #198).
* New `Turn on Thoughts` switch in Hushfeed settings > App. It shows Thoughts on profiles and in your inbox, plus the prompt to share one, for accounts TikTok left out. It starts off, and TikTok's servers can still refuse a post (#186).
* `Keep photos as TikTok sent them` now also covers stickers that don't move, and `Download original photos` keeps TikTok's own file when it's on (#229).
* `Keep the screen's brightness in the camera` now also covers the front flash and the fill light, which used to push the screen to full brightness on their own. The flash still turns the screen white, just at your own brightness (#200).

## Update

Refresh the Hushfeed source in Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer and patch TikTok again. Keep the manager's existing signing key so your login and settings carry over. The .mpp is a patch bundle, not a TikTok APK.

## Checked

* This exact bundle was patched onto TikTok 47.5.3 and run on a signed-in emulator. A walk through the whole app opened all 27 of its screens with no crash.
* Every patch applied to TikTok 47.5.3, and 94 applied to PineDrama 47.5.3 with none failing.
* An imported font drew PineDrama's settings and its drama feed after a restart, and bold titles stayed bold (#243).
* Sorting @natgeo's grid oldest first kept loading on its own up to 300 videos, and a tapped video opened that same video (#180).
* `Save the frame on screen as a photo` saved clean 720x1280 frames from a For You video and from a profile video.
* With `Automatic Clear display` on, a search result opened a second time cleared again (#84).
* With `Double tap` set to `Do nothing`, a tap paused or played in 8 to 43 ms, and two taps 150 ms apart paused and then played (#239).
